statement: At fixed d and high accuracy, SAQNN matches the d/s parameter exponent of the Sobolev n-width; at fixed non-tiny accuracy and sufficiently high d, its displayed circuit size is asymptotically below the cited ReLU-FNN size.
scope_controls: The circuit-size advantage is not claimed uniformly as epsilon tends to zero at fixed d.
The parameter-rate comparison uses the source Case-4 Fourier rate, not the loose uniform sufficient-n display.
